translations.answer: The thread participants wrote the floating base equations using mass matrix, nonlinear terms, and foot Jacobian. The original author then stated that the method is very close to direct RNEA results. Project members also pointed out that this hand-written combination does not exploit the sparsity of the kinematic tree, and the CRBA algorithm is more complex than RNEA, so it should not be used as a regular inverse dynamics implementation. Since the original thread did not provide error or benchmark, it can only be used as a cross-check path and not for quantifying speed differences or ensuring numerical equivalence.
translations.applicability: Applicable to original post quadruped inverse-dynamics cross-check; whether real-time WBC is acceptable must be benchmarked on the target dimension and implementation.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Maintainer suggests using kMt.act(f_t); the author then uses the parent-joint force/wrench from OCS2 fixed submission.
translations.details.attempts.1: Another participant wrote the floating base equations using CRBA, nonLinearEffects, and frame Jacobians, and the original author compared it with RNEA results.
translations.details.attempts.2: Participants discussed the solution boundaries for single-contact re-rooting and multi-contact acceleration-level holonomic constraints.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First find the parent joint and relative placement of the contact frame, then transform the wrench to the joint local frame.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Distinguish between a single force element and a force vector of length model.njoints.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Compare the hand-written floating base equations with RNEA output, and separately evaluate whether the kinematic-tree sparsity was utilized.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Establish a fext element based on the contact frame's parent joint, transform the world-frame force to the joint frame, and construct the moment using joint-to-contact translation × force; add 6D contact and joint-frame contact torque.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: Apply the transformation to a single pinocchio::Force, not to aligned_vector<Force>.
translations.details.environments.0: 2022 Pinocchio C++; floating-base quadruped; foot-tip contact frames; author ultimately used the CentroidalModelRbdConversions.cpp from OCS2 commit 3566993.
translations.details.limits.0: The original author's reference OCS2 code is based on specific centroidal input and contact metadata; prior to copying, one must verify the frame parent, wrench order, and coordinate expression.
translations.details.limits.1: The thread does not provide specific Pinocchio release, numerical error, or runtime measurement.
translations.details.limits.2: The discussion about re-rooting, Schur complement, and TSID in multi-contact scenarios is architectural suggestion, not a completed implementation in this thread.
translations.details.limits.3: The original author's statement about ignoring the first six dimensions of RNEA depends on their system interpretation; the thread does not validate it as a universal operation for all floating-base robots.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The original author confirmed the issue is resolved after using the referenced OCS2 code.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The original author reported the hand-written floating base equations are very close to RNEA but did not provide error or speed benchmark.
translations.details.outcomes.2: The multi-contact QP/TSID design discussion is not provided in this thread for implementation verification.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How to construct the RNEA fext in the joint local frame when there is no joint at the foot tip?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Does using CRBA, nonLinearEffects, and frame Jacobian to write the contact inverse dynamics equate to RNEA and is it efficient?
translations.details.problem_statements.2: Can the zero velocity/acceleration constraints for multiple fixed contact points be handled by setting one contact point as the RNEA root?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before outputting the contact moment from an actual robot, verify the sign of fext, reference point, frame transform, and residual from unactuated base dynamics.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Directly inputting the contact-frame force into RNEA without transforming the action point or local expression.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Calling SE3 action on an entire std::vector<Force> instead of the correct SE3 action for a single Force.
translations.details.suspected_causes.2: Hand-writting CRBA/Jacobian calculations without leveraging RNEA's kinematic tree recursive sparsity.
translations.details.symptoms.0: RNEA requires a local-frame fext for each joint, but physical contact occurs in a foot-tip frame without a joint.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Calling SE3 act on aligned_vector<Force> causes a compilation error, as the vector lacks a se3Action.
